+@contextmanager
+def pause_after_git(process, arguments, *, transaction_open=False):
+    """Schedule an external writer after a real Git child finishes its read.
+
+    Only the CLI owner is suspended. Its Git child can finish, leaving its result
+    unread until the caller resumes the owner. Bound observation and always resume
+    before the foreground fixture performs its normal process cleanup.
+    """
+    children = Path(f"/proc/{process.pid}/task/{process.pid}/children")
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 20
+    paused = False
+    scheduled = False
+    try:
+        while time.monotonic() < deadline and process.poll() is None:
+            for child in children.read_text().split():
+                try:
+                    command = Path(f"/proc/{child}/cmdline").read_bytes().split(b"\0")
+                    if command[0] != b"git" or command[-len(arguments) - 1 : -1] != [
+                        part.encode() for part in arguments
+                    ]:
+                        continue
+                    os.kill(process.pid, signal.SIGSTOP)
+                    paused = True
+                    commands = [
+                        Path(f"/proc/{pid}/cmdline").read_bytes().split(b"\0")
+                        for pid in children.read_text().split()
+                    ]
+                    if (
+                        any(c[-3:-1] == [b"update-ref", b"--stdin"] for c in commands)
+                        != transaction_open
+                    ):
+                        continue
+                    # The owner cannot reap this child once stopped. If it already
+                    # did, resume and keep looking rather than claim a schedule.
+                    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+                        state = Path(f"/proc/{child}/stat").read_text().split(") ", 1)[1][0]
+                        if state == "Z":
+                            scheduled = True
+                            break
+                        time.sleep(0.001)
+                except (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError):
+                    pass
+                finally:
+                    if paused and not scheduled:
+                        os.kill(process.pid, signal.SIGCONT)
+                        paused = False
+                if scheduled:
+                    break
+            if scheduled:
+                break
+        if not scheduled:
+            raise AssertionError(f"Did not observe Git command {arguments}")
+        yield
+    finally:
+        if paused:
+            os.kill(process.pid, signal.SIGCONT)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("after_prepare", [False, True])
+def test_development_alias_after_validation_cannot_follow_automatic_integration(
+    graph, after_prepare
+):
+    configure_plan(graph)
+    with foreground(graph) as process:
+        # Exclude setup checks; the first candidate is already tested when this
+        # final destination read runs. This is the original Spec02 interleaving.
+        wait_for(
+            graph,
+            process,
+            lambda record: any(g["stage"] == "candidate" for g in record["gates"]),
+        )
+        with pause_after_git(
+            process,
+            ["for-each-ref", "--format=%(symref)", "refs/heads/dev"],
+            transaction_open=after_prepare,
+        ):
+            before = graph.git("show-ref")
+            mutation = subprocess.run(
+                [
+                    "git",
+                    "-C",
+                    str(graph.repo),
+                    "symbolic-ref",
+                    "refs/heads/dev",
+                    "refs/heads/integration",
+                ],
+                capture_output=True,
+                text=True,
+            )
+            assert mutation.returncode == (1 if after_prepare else 0), mutation.stderr
+            assert graph.git("show-ref") == before
+        record = wait_for(
+            graph,
+            process,
+            lambda record: record["outcome"] in ("incomplete", "awaiting_human_qa"),
+        )
+        assert graph.git("rev-parse", "dev") == graph.base
+        assert record.get("qa_decisions", []) == []
+        if mutation.returncode == 0:
+            assert record["failure"]["stage"] == "integration"
+            assert record["tickets"]["03"]["state"] == "Blocked"
+            assert graph.git("rev-parse", "integration") == graph.base
+            assert not (graph.output / "qa-request.json").exists()
+            process.wait(timeout=10)
+            # Abort must release both refs for subsequent ordinary Git writers.
+            graph.git("update-ref", "--no-deref", "refs/heads/dev", graph.base)
+            graph.git("update-ref", "refs/heads/integration", graph.base, graph.base)
+        else:
+            assert "lock" in mutation.stderr.lower()
+            assert record["outcome"] == "awaiting_human_qa"
+            assert graph.git("rev-parse", "integration") != graph.base
+
+

+def _transaction_exchange(process: subprocess.Popen[bytes], command: str, expected: bytes) -> None:
+    """Read Git's protocol acknowledgement without buffering or stderr deadlocks."""
+    assert process.stdin is not None and process.stdout is not None
+    process.stdin.write(command.encode())
+    process.stdin.flush()
+    observed = b""
+    while observed != expected:
+        chunk = os.read(process.stdout.fileno(), 4096)
+        observed += chunk
+        if not chunk or not expected.startswith(observed):
+            raise GateFailure("Git ref transaction rejected: " + observed.decode(errors="replace"))
+
+
+def _update_direct_branches(
+    repository: Path, refs: dict[str, tuple[str | None, str]], failure: str
+) -> None:
+    """Hold all destination locks while validating topology, then commit together.
+
+    A verify entry holds a read-only ref alongside updates. OID verification with
+    no-deref alone still accepts same-OID symbolic refs; validate topology after
+    prepare, when ordinary Git writers cannot replace any of these names.
+    """
+    commands = "start\n"
+    for branch, (revision, previous) in refs.items():
+        commands += "option no-deref\n"
+        commands += (
+            f"update refs/heads/{branch} {revision} {previous}\n"
+            if revision is not None
+            else f"verify refs/heads/{branch} {previous}\n"
+        )
+    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as diagnostic:
+        process = subprocess.Popen(
+            [
+                "git",
+                "-C",
+                str(repository),
+                "-c",
+                "core.hooksPath=/dev/null",
+                "update-ref",
+                "--stdin",
+            ],
+            stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
+            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+            stderr=diagnostic,
+            bufsize=0,
+        )
+        try:
+            _transaction_exchange(process, commands + "prepare\n", b"start: ok\nprepare: ok\n")
+            require_direct_branches(repository, *refs)
+            _transaction_exchange(process, "commit\n", b"commit: ok\n")
+            assert process.stdin is not None
+            process.stdin.close()
+            process.stdin = None
+            process.wait()
+            if process.returncode:
+                raise GateFailure("Git ref transaction failed")
+        except (GateFailure, OSError) as error:
+            diagnostic.seek(0)
+            detail = diagnostic.read().decode(errors="replace").strip()
+            raise GateFailure(f"{failure}: {error}" + (f"\n{detail}" if detail else "")) from error
+        finally:
+            # An uncommitted transaction is explicitly aborted; EOF is Git's
+            # fallback abort if it already rejected input or the pipe is broken.
+            try:
+                process.communicate(
+                    input=b"abort\n" if process.poll() is None else None, timeout=10
+                )
+            except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
+                process.kill()
+                process.communicate()
